{{recipesummary|category=Chinese recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}}

'''Steamed pork with mustard greens''' (梅菜扣肉, pinyin: Méicàikòuròu) or '''mei cai kou rou''' is a Chinese dish from the Hakka people. It is very popular and tasty but contains a lot of saturated fat.

==Ingredients==
* About 10.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Mustard Greens|mustard greens]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:cornstarch|cornstarch]] combined with 1 tsp cold water
* ½ tsp [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2 tsp light [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 1 tsp rice [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] or water
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] [[Cookbook:pork|pork]] tenderloin
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Black Bean Sauce|black bean and garlic sauce]]
* About 2 tbsp water
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Wash greens and discard tough stems. 
# Bring a large pot of water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], add greens, and cook for 2 minutes. 
# Drain greens and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking. Drain again, then cut greens into long diagonal strips.
# In a medium bowl, combine cornstarch and water. Stir in sugar, soy sauce and rice wine. Cut pork into thin slices and add to the mixture. [[Cookbook:Marinating|Marinate]] about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
# Heat oil in a preheated [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]] or large heavy [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat. Add black bean sauce and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir-fry]] for 1 minute.
# Add pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes. 
# Add mustard greens and water. Mix well and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] gently about 4–5 minutes, until pork is cooked through and greens are tender.
# Season with pepper and serve.

==References==
* Hsiung, Deh-Ta. ''The Chinese Kitchen: A Book of Essential Ingredients with Over 200 Easy and Authentic Recipes''. New York: St. Martin's Griffin, 2002.
